chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A branch of the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and they greeted him, so he returned the greeting to them. They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we have a need for you.' He said, 'Present your need.' They said, 'It is a great need.' He said, 'Present it, what is it?' They said, 'Guarantee for us Paradise upon your Lord.'

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) lowered his head, then struck the ground with his finger, then raised his head and said, 'I will do that for you on the condition that you do not ask anyone for anything.'

So it was that a man from them would be traveling, and his whip would fall, so he would dislike saying to a person, 'Hand it to me,' fleeing from asking, so he would dismount and take it himself. And he would be at the table, and one of the seated would be closer to the water than him, so he would not say, 'Hand it to me,' until he would stand up and drink.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَار: The Helpers (a specific tribe in Medina)
key_terms.الْمَائِدَة: A table or place of sitting/eating
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَة: Asking for something, specifically begging or requesting from others
key_terms.فَخِذ: A branch or division of a tribe

ai.seo_question: What condition did the Prophet set when guaranteeing the Ansar Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the theological link between self-sufficiency (Istighna) and the guarantee of Paradise, a concept central to Shia ethical teachings on dignity. The Prophet’s condition highlights that avoiding the humiliation of asking others is a spiritual discipline that preserves one's independence from creation, reflecting the principle of 'asking only from God'. This narrative serves as a foundational text for the Shia jurisprudence and ethics of begging, emphasizing that true reliance on God (Tawakkul) manifests in practical self-reliance.
